claims: Russell George v. Costco was filed against Costco in early April 2026.
Russell George v. Costco is a class-action lawsuit.
Russell George v. Costco was filed by California resident Russell George.
Russell George v. Costco alleges violations of California's Automatic Renewal Law (ARL).
Russell George v. Costco alleges violations of California's False Advertising Law.
Russell George v. Costco alleges violations of California's Unfair Competition Law.
Russell George v. Costco alleges violations of California's Consumers Legal Remedies Act.
Russell George v. Costco alleges that Costco sends membership renewal notices 60 days in advance.
California's Automatic Renewal Law (ARL) requires a 15 to 45-day window for membership renewal notices.
Russell George v. Costco claims that sending notices 60 days in advance prevented customers from easily canceling.
Russell George v. Costco claims that the early notice resulted in automatic charges of $65 for renewals the user did not want.
Russell George v. Costco seeks damages.
Russell George v. Costco seeks a jury trial.
Russell George v. Costco seeks class-action status.
A preliminary hearing for Russell George v. Costco is slated for June 2026.
